_meta.description: Every CNY-to-USD channel identified. Null means the value could NOT be confirmed from an official source and is flagged. Nothing is inferred.
_meta.critical_distinction: Chinese FX law splits individuals into 境内个人 (domestic) and 境外个人 (non-domestic). Under State Council Order 532 Art. 52(2), a foreigner who has resided in China continuously for one year IS a domestic individual. This single fact decides which rule set applies to a US citizen.

status_legend.legal: Expressly provided for in an official rule
status_legend.legal_conditional: Lawful only if the stated conditions and documents are met
status_legend.prohibited: Expressly prohibited or penalised by an official rule
status_legend.unverified: Existence or terms could not be confirmed from an official source

methods.name: Convert lawful RMB income to USD as a non-domestic individual (境外个人), then wire
methods.who: US citizen who has NOT resided continuously in China for a full year
methods.how: Art. 13(1): RMB income lawfully earned under the current account in China is converted at the bank on presentation of valid ID plus supporting documents evidencing the transaction amount, including tax payment vouchers. The USD is then remitted under Art. 15.
methods.limit_text: No annual quota is imposed on this route by Art. 13. The amount is bounded by the documented lawful income, not by a fixed cap. The USD 50,000 annual total in Art. 2 applies to settlement by individuals and to purchase by DOMESTIC individuals only.
methods.documents: Valid ID; documents evidencing the transaction amount; tax payment vouchers (税务凭证)
methods.china_cost: Bank FX spread plus remittance tariff. Bank of China charges no separate fee for FX exchange at its own branches (S12 item 210107011); remittance tariff at S12 item 210105008.
methods.us_tax: Not income merely because it is transferred. But a currency gain on disposition of the RMB can be ordinary income under IRC 988 (S19). FBAR / Form 8938 apply to the account.
pros: Not subject to the USD 50,000 annual purchase quota, because Art. 2 limits purchase only for domestic individuals
Uses the ordinary banking system, so a clean documentary trail exists
No Chinese tax arises on the conversion itself; tax was due on the underlying income when earned
cons: Requires tax vouchers proving the income was declared in China; undocumented savings cannot use it
Only covers current-account income, not capital such as property sale proceeds
Bank must perform authenticity review and may refuse if documents are incomplete

methods.name: Purchase FX within the USD 50,000 annual total, then wire (domestic individual)
methods.who: Chinese citizens, and foreigners who HAVE resided in China continuously for one year (Order 532 Art. 52(2))
methods.how: Art. 2: within the annual total, purchase is handled at the bank on valid ID alone. Art. 3: the FX purchased may be remitted abroad, deposited to the person's own FX savings account, or carried out subject to the banknote rules.
methods.limit_text: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year for purchase by a domestic individual (Art. 2). SAFE may adjust the annual total.
methods.documents: Valid personal identity document only, while within the annual total
methods.china_cost: Bank FX spread plus remittance tariff (S12). No Chinese tax on the act of conversion.
methods.us_tax: Transfer of own funds is not itself income; IRC 988 currency gain may still arise (S19). FBAR / Form 8938 apply.
pros: Minimal paperwork inside the quota: ID only
Predictable and repeatable each calendar year
Cheapest documented channel for amounts at or below the quota
cons: Hard annual ceiling; large balances take multiple years
Borrowing or lending quota to move more is expressly policed and leads to watch-listing (S03)
A US citizen who has lived in China a year is caught by this cap, which many guides get wrong

methods.name: Above-quota current-account purchase with transaction documents (domestic individual)
methods.who: Domestic individuals whose genuine current-account need exceeds USD 50,000
methods.how: Art. 2 and Art. 12: above the annual total, a domestic individual purchases FX for non-business current-account purposes at the bank on valid ID plus supporting documents evidencing the transaction amount.
methods.limit_text: No fixed ceiling stated; bounded by the documented genuine transaction amount. Art. 12 sets a documentary test, not a numeric cap.
methods.documents: Valid ID plus documents evidencing the transaction amount for the current-account purpose
methods.china_cost: Bank FX spread plus remittance tariff (S12)
methods.us_tax: Same analysis as M02
pros: Lawful way to exceed USD 50,000 in a single year
No SAFE pre-approval needed for current-account items handled at the bank
cons: Only for genuine current-account purposes; it is not a route for moving investment capital
Bank performs authenticity review under Art. 6 and must reject fabricated transactions
False or invalid documents convert this into illegal arbitrage under Order 532 Art. 40

methods.name: Remit FX already held in your own foreign-currency savings account
methods.who: Any individual holding USD or other FX in a Chinese FX savings account
methods.how: Art. 15(1): a non-domestic individual remits FX from an FX savings account abroad on valid ID alone. Art. 14: a domestic individual may remit up to USD 50,000 equivalent per day on ID alone; above that, current-account authenticity vouchers are required.
methods.limit_text: Non-domestic individual: no numeric cap stated in Art. 15(1) for remitting FX from a savings account. Domestic individual: USD 50,000 equivalent PER DAY on ID alone (Art. 14), above which documents are needed. This daily threshold is separate from the annual purchase quota.
methods.documents: Non-domestic: valid ID. Domestic: valid ID up to USD 50,000 per day; authenticity vouchers above.
methods.china_cost: Remittance tariff only; no conversion needed if the balance is already USD (S12)
methods.us_tax: No conversion means no new IRC 988 disposition at this step. FBAR / Form 8938 still apply.
pros: If the money is already in USD, the FX spread is avoided entirely
For a non-domestic individual Art. 15(1) states no numeric ceiling
The daily USD 50,000 threshold for domestic individuals is far less restrictive than the annual purchase quota
cons: Only helps if the balance is already in foreign currency
Converting RMB into that FX account first still triggers the purchase rules in M01/M02/M03

methods.name: Inheritance transfer (继承财产转移) — repatriating a Chinese estate you inherited
methods.who: A foreign citizen who has lawfully inherited an estate located in China
methods.how: PBOC [2004] No. 16 Art. 2 and Art. 9: the heir liquidates the inherited domestic estate, applies to SAFE at the decedent's former household-registration locality, then purchases and remits FX through a designated bank. Now administered under Huifa [2024] No. 12 s.6.4.
methods.limit_text: No annual quota. Approval threshold: total at or below RMB 500,000 equivalent is approved by the local SAFE branch; above that the branch reviews and forwards to SAFE head office (Art. 10). Estate from one decedent must be applied for in one application but may be remitted in one or several instalments (Art. 6).
methods.documents: Written application; FX business application form; identity documents; proof of overseas residence issued or authenticated by a Chinese embassy/consulate; proof of entitlement to the inherited property; the decedent's property title documents; tax certificate or tax payment voucher from the competent tax authority at the property's location; notarisation where required (Art. 9)
methods.china_cost: Bank FX spread plus remittance tariff. Notary and document costs apply but no official schedule was verified.
methods.us_tax: An inheritance is generally not income to the recipient, but Form 3520 Part IV applies above USD 100,000 from a foreign estate (S17). Income earned by the estate and currency gain can still be reportable.
pros: Purpose-built lawful channel for exactly the 'money stuck in China' problem where the money is inherited
No USD 50,000 annual ceiling and no staged-remittance rule for a single decedent's estate
Explicitly open to foreign citizens, so US citizenship is not an obstacle
cons: Requires a tax certificate for the decedent's property, which is often the practical bottleneck
SAFE will not accept the application if the property is subject to judicial restriction or pending criminal or civil proceedings (Art. 12)
Art. 11 forbids taking the proceeds out as banknotes in China; funds must go to the heir's own account abroad
Cannot prove lawful source of funds means refusal (Art. 12)

methods.name: Emigration transfer (移民财产转移) — moving pre-emigration assets out
methods.who: A natural person who emigrated from mainland China to a foreign country, or settled in Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan
methods.how: PBOC [2004] No. 16 Art. 2 and Art. 8: liquidate lawful property owned in China BEFORE acquiring immigrant status, apply to SAFE at the former household-registration locality, then purchase and remit through a designated bank.
methods.limit_text: No annual quota, but staged remittance under Art. 6: first remittance no more than half the approved total; after one year no more than half the remainder; after two years the entire remainder. If the whole approved amount is RMB 200,000 equivalent or less it may be remitted in one lump sum. Art. 10 approval split at RMB 500,000.
methods.documents: Written application explaining reason and source of property; applicant information form; FX business application form; Chinese household-registration cancellation certificate issued by public security; proof of overseas settlement issued or authenticated by a Chinese embassy/consulate; property title documents such as title deeds, sale contracts or relocation compensation agreements; notarised agency agreement if applicable (Art. 8)
methods.china_cost: Bank FX spread plus remittance tariff. Note IIT Art. 10(5) and Art. 13 require tax clearance before household-registration cancellation (S11).
methods.us_tax: Transfer of own capital is not itself income. IRC 988 currency gain and FBAR / Form 8938 still apply.
pros: The only general-purpose lawful channel for moving a large pre-emigration capital balance
No USD 50,000 annual ceiling
cons: Requires a Chinese household-registration cancellation certificate, so it is unavailable to a US citizen who never held Chinese hukou
Only covers property owned BEFORE immigrant status was acquired
Staged remittance can take two years for larger amounts
Same judicial-restriction and lawful-source bars as M05 (Art. 12)

methods.name: Remit RMB offshore under the current account, then convert to USD outside China
methods.who: Individuals with lawful current-account income such as salary
methods.how: Yinfa [2020] No. 330 item 13 supports domestic banks handling individuals' current-account cross-border RMB settlement, expressly facilitating cross-border receipt and payment of salary and other lawful income. The RMB leaves as RMB; conversion to USD happens at the receiving bank offshore.
methods.documents: Bank applies the 'three principles of business conduct' (展业三原则) authenticity review. A specific document list for individuals is not set out in item 13.
methods.china_cost: No onshore CNY-to-USD conversion, so the onshore FX spread is avoided. Offshore conversion spread and bank charges were not verified from an official source.
methods.us_tax: Receiving RMB does not avoid US tax. Converting RMB to USD offshore is still a disposition of nonfunctional currency under IRC 988 (S19).
pros: Avoids the onshore individual FX purchase quota entirely, because no onshore conversion takes place
Expressly supported by a six-ministry PBOC notice for salary and other lawful income
Offshore conversion is not restricted by SAFE rules once the RMB has lawfully left
cons: Bank must still verify the underlying transaction is genuine and current-account
Whether a given bank offers this to a given customer, and any per-transaction cap, could not be confirmed from an official source
Does not solve the problem for capital balances such as property sale proceeds

methods.name: Carry foreign-currency banknotes out of China
methods.who: Any departing traveller
methods.how: Huifa [2003] No. 102 covering notice item 2: up to USD 5,000 equivalent needs no permit; above USD 5,000 up to USD 10,000 needs a Carrying Permit issued by a designated bank; in principle no more than USD 10,000 may be carried out, and only specified special circumstances allow a permit from SAFE above that.
methods.limit_text: Per trip: USD 5,000 equivalent permit-free; USD 5,000-10,000 with bank-issued permit; above USD 10,000 in principle not permitted, SAFE permit only for listed special cases. Separate stricter tiers apply to same-day and 15-day repeat crossers.
methods.documents: Carrying Permit (携带证) stamped by the bank or SAFE above the permit-free tier
methods.china_cost: Bank of China lists the FX carrying permit at RMB 10 but waives the fee from 2025-04-01 to 2026-12-31 (S12 item 210101002). Cash conversion spread still applies.
methods.us_tax: Entering the US with more than USD 10,000 requires FinCEN Form 105; the threshold aggregates families and groups (S21). Carrying is not itself taxable.
pros: Immediately available for small amounts without a wire
Permit fee currently waived at Bank of China
cons: Effectively capped near USD 10,000 per trip, so useless for a large balance
Repeat crossings are pushed into much lower tiers, so repeated runs are not a workaround
Carrying in breach is penalised under Order 532 Art. 42 and by Customs
Loss or theft risk; US declaration duty on arrival

methods.name: Carry RMB banknotes out of China
methods.who: Chinese citizens and foreigners alike
methods.how: Customs confirms a limit of RMB 20,000 per person per trip. Amounts above the limit are not released.
methods.limit_text: RMB 20,000 per person per trip, excluding same-day and short-period repeat crossers (S05).
methods.china_cost: No conversion occurs in China; RMB must be converted after arrival, at an unverified offshore spread.
methods.us_tax: RMB is nonfunctional currency; converting it after arrival is an IRC 988 disposition (S19). Over USD 10,000 equivalent entering the US requires FinCEN 105 (S21).
pros: Simple for very small amounts
cons: RMB 20,000 is a trivial ceiling
RMB is not freely convertible everywhere, so the offshore rate may be worse
Excess is not released by Customs

methods.name: Bank draft (票汇) and clean collection (光票托收)
methods.who: Individuals able to visit a branch
methods.how: A bank draft is a negotiable instrument carried or mailed abroad and presented for payment. Huifa [2003] No. 102 notice item 3 states Customs no longer controls the carrying of foreign-currency payment instruments and securities. Bank of China publishes tariffs for both cross-border draft remittance and clean collection.
methods.limit_text: The underlying FX purchase remains subject to whichever of M01/M02/M03 applies. No separate instrument-specific quota was found.
methods.documents: As required for the underlying purchase; draft presentation abroad
methods.china_cost: Draft remittance: 0.1% of amount, min RMB 50, max RMB 260, plus postage if any. Clean collection: 0.1%, min RMB 50, max RMB 250, plus actual postage; RMB 10 return fee if the overseas bank returns it (S12 items 210105008, 210106010).
methods.us_tax: A bearer or unrestrictedly endorsed instrument over USD 10,000 is a monetary instrument for FinCEN 105 (S21).
pros: Carrying a draft is not subject to the banknote carrying-permit tiers
Published, capped tariff
cons: Slow clearing; the paying bank may return the item
Still counts toward US monetary-instrument reporting if physically carried
Underlying purchase quota is unchanged

methods.name: Spend or withdraw abroad on a China-issued card
methods.who: Holder of a Chinese debit or credit card travelling abroad
methods.how: Value leaves as overseas spending or ATM cash rather than as a remittance. Bank of China publishes a cross-border ATM withdrawal tariff. Art. 35(5) of the Detailed Rules excludes domestic-card overseas use with FX repayment from the individual FX system.
methods.china_cost: Bank of China Great Wall debit card cross-border ATM: RMB 12 plus 1% of the withdrawal, capped at RMB 112 per transaction. Some overseas ATM operators add a surcharge (S12 item 210108014 and note 10).
methods.us_tax: Spending is not a remittance, but converting RMB is still an IRC 988 disposition (S19). The account remains FBAR / Form 8938 reportable.
pros: Practical for living costs rather than capital transfer
Published per-transaction fee cap
cons: An annual aggregate overseas cash-withdrawal cap is widely described but could not be confirmed from an official source in this session, so it is left blank and flagged
1% plus a fixed fee is expensive at scale
Not a capital repatriation route

methods.name: International money-transfer operator via a Chinese bank agent
methods.who: Individuals using an operator desk or a bank channel acting as agent
methods.how: Bank of China's tariff note 6 confirms it handles cross-border outward remittance as agent for international remittance companies, that the charges are collected on their behalf, and that the pricing is set by those companies.
methods.us_tax: Transfer of own funds is not income. FBAR / Form 8938 apply to the account; IRC 988 may apply to the conversion.
pros: Fast payout and wide agent coverage
The agency relationship itself is confirmed in an official bank tariff
cons: Operator-set fees and per-transfer limits are not published in the official tariff and could not be verified
The underlying FX purchase is still governed by SAFE rules, so it does not create extra quota

methods.name: Qualified Domestic Institutional Investor (QDII) outbound investment
methods.who: Domestic individuals investing through a bank or fund manager
methods.how: Art. 17: a domestic individual may use FX or RMB to make overseas fixed-income and equity investments through a qualified domestic institutional investor such as a bank or fund management company.
methods.documents: Institution-specific onboarding; the institution holds the quota
methods.us_tax: A US person investing in a non-US pooled fund commonly triggers PFIC reporting on Form 8621. That analysis was not verified in this session and is flagged.
pros: Lawful outbound investment channel expressly recognised in Art. 17
cons: This invests money offshore; it is not a clean route to cash in your own US bank account
Institution-level quota and product terms were not verified
Potential PFIC complexity for US persons

methods.name: Overseas-listed company employee share plan proceeds
methods.who: Domestic individuals participating in an overseas listed company's employee share or option plan
methods.how: Art. 18: the company or its domestic agent applies to SAFE collectively. Proceeds of share sales and dividends are remitted back to a dedicated domestic FX account, then may be settled or transferred into the employee's own FX savings account.
methods.limit_text: Governed by the approved plan, not by the USD 50,000 individual purchase quota
methods.documents: Employer or domestic agency applies to SAFE on the employee's behalf
methods.us_tax: Share-plan income is compensation or capital gain and is separately reportable; the FX leg can also carry IRC 988 gain.
pros: Once proceeds sit in the employee's own FX savings account, M04 governs the outward remittance
Outside the individual annual purchase quota
cons: Only available to participants of an approved plan
Requires employer cooperation and SAFE approval

methods.name: Outbound direct investment (ODI) with SAFE approval and registration
methods.who: Domestic individuals making a genuine overseas direct investment
methods.how: Art. 16: outbound direct investment by a domestic individual follows the relevant state rules; the FX needed may be purchased or remitted from own FX after approval by the local SAFE bureau, with corresponding outbound investment FX registration.
methods.documents: SAFE approval; outbound investment FX registration; approval or filing from the competent commerce authority where required
methods.us_tax: A US person owning a foreign corporation may face Form 5471 and related regimes. Not verified in this session.
pros: Lawful capital-account channel where there is a genuine investment
cons: Requires a real overseas business; it is not a personal cash repatriation route
Order 532 Art. 44 penalises changing the approved use of capital-account funds
Heavy US entity-reporting burden

methods.name: Family support and donation receipts above the quota, with documents
methods.who: Domestic individuals receiving genuine family support or donations from abroad
methods.how: Art. 10 lists the documentary basis for above-quota settlement, including notarised donation agreements and family-support evidence such as proof of relationship and the overseas payer's income or tax records.
methods.limit_text: No fixed cap stated; bounded by the documented genuine amount
methods.documents: Donation: notarised donation agreement or contract. Family support: proof of direct family relationship or notarised support relationship, plus the overseas payer's income evidence such as bank deposit proof or tax vouchers (Art. 10(1)-(2)).
methods.china_cost: Bank FX spread; notary costs not verified
methods.us_tax: Note this is an INBOUND route. A US person receiving a gift from a foreign person above USD 100,000 files Form 3520 Part IV (S17).
pros: Documented route for genuine cross-border family transfers
cons: Runs in the wrong direction for someone trying to get money OUT of China
Fabricating a donation to move funds is illegal arbitrage under Order 532 Art. 40

methods.name: Personal foreign-trade operator settlement account
methods.who: An individual who has registered as a personal foreign-trade operator with trading rights
methods.how: Art. 9(1): a personal foreign-trade operator conducts trade-related FX purchase, payment, receipt and settlement through their own FX settlement account, with receipts and payments managed as for an institution.
methods.limit_text: Managed under institutional rules rather than the individual annual total
methods.documents: Business licence or other practice certificate; commerce-authority filing conferring foreign-trade operating rights
methods.us_tax: Trade income is taxable business income; a US person may face Schedule C and foreign entity reporting.
pros: Genuine trade flows sit outside the USD 50,000 individual quota
cons: Requires a real registered trading business with real goods flows
Using a trade shell with fabricated invoices is expressly penalised (Order 532 Art. 40)

methods.name: Underground money changer / underground bank (地下钱庄), including mirror '对敲' settlement
methods.who: Anyone
methods.how: RMB is paid to a broker inside China and foreign currency is paid out to you outside China, with no cross-border flow through the banking system.
methods.china_cost: Order 532 Art. 45: warning, confiscation of illegal gains, and a fine of up to 30% of the illegal amount; in serious circumstances a fine of 30% up to 100% of the illegal amount; criminal liability where a crime is constituted.
methods.us_tax: US reporting duties are unchanged and receiving funds from an unlicensed changer adds money-laundering exposure.
cons: Expressly prohibited; fine can reach the full amount moved in serious cases
Criminal liability where a crime is constituted
No recourse if the broker simply keeps the money
Funds may be frozen and the receiving US account closed

methods.name: Quota splitting or borrowing other people's USD 50,000 allowances ('ants moving')
methods.who: Anyone
methods.how: Several individuals each purchase FX within their own annual total and pool it to one overseas recipient, or one person lends their quota to another.
methods.limit_text: Huifa [2015] No. 49 item 2 expressly forbids evading quota and authenticity management by splitting.
methods.china_cost: Watch-listing: the year of listing plus the following two consecutive years, during which every purchase or settlement requires documentary proof at the counter. Underlying evasion or illegal arbitrage is separately fined under Order 532 Art. 39 or Art. 40 at up to 30%, or 30%-100% in serious cases.
methods.us_tax: Unchanged; structuring may additionally breach US rules.
cons: Both the borrower and the lender of quota are targeted; a first-time lender gets a risk warning and a repeat lender is listed
Three years of losing counter-free processing
Exposure to evasion and arbitrage fines on top

methods.name: Cryptocurrency or stablecoin P2P (e.g. buying USDT with CNY)
methods.who: Anyone
methods.how: Buy crypto peer-to-peer with RMB, transfer the asset, sell for USD abroad.
methods.china_cost: Yinfa [2021] No. 237 item 1(2) classifies fiat-to-virtual-currency exchange as an illegal financial activity, strictly prohibited and to be banned; item 1(3) extends this to overseas exchanges serving mainland residents; item 1(4) provides that related civil acts contrary to public order are void and losses are borne by the participant.
methods.us_tax: Crypto is property for US purposes; the sale is a taxable disposal. FBAR treatment of virtual currency is a separate question not resolved here.
cons: Expressly illegal in China; criminal liability where a crime is constituted
Banks and payment institutions are forbidden from providing accounts or settlement for it, so accounts used are at risk
Civil transactions may be void, leaving no legal recourse for losses
Counterparty fraud and price risk between legs

methods.name: Trade mis-invoicing or false documents to purchase FX
methods.who: Anyone
methods.how: Present fabricated or inflated contracts or invoices to a bank to obtain FX or move value under a false trade purpose.
methods.china_cost: Order 532 Art. 40: order to re-exchange the funds plus a fine of up to 30% of the illegally arbitrated amount; in serious circumstances 30% up to 100%; criminal liability where a crime is constituted. Art. 39 covers evasion by transferring domestic FX abroad in breach of rules on the same fine scale.
methods.us_tax: False records create separate US exposure.
cons: Bank authenticity review under Art. 6 is designed to catch exactly this
Fines can reach the entire amount in serious cases
Criminal exposure

methods.name: Carrying cash above the permit tiers or failing to declare
methods.who: Any traveller
methods.how: Taking out more than the permitted banknote amount, or splitting cash across companions or trips to stay under a threshold.
methods.limit_text: See M08 for the lawful tiers
methods.china_cost: Order 532 Art. 42: warning and a possible fine of up to 20% of the illegal amount; where laws or administrative regulations assign the penalty to Customs, those provisions prevail.
methods.us_tax: On the US side, failure to file FinCEN 105 risks forfeiture and seizure of the currency plus civil or criminal penalties (S21).
cons: Chinese fine up to 20% plus Customs treatment
US forfeiture can reach the whole amount, not just the excess
Repeat-crossing rules defeat the split-across-trips approach

methods.name: Operating an unlicensed FX settlement or sale business
methods.who: Anyone acting as the changer rather than the customer
methods.how: Running a conversion service without approval.
methods.china_cost: Order 532 Art. 46: confiscation of illegal gains; where gains are RMB 500,000 or more a fine of 1 to 5 times the gains; where there are no gains or gains are under RMB 500,000 a fine of RMB 500,000 to 2,000,000; serious cases lose the licence; criminal liability where a crime is constituted.
methods.us_tax: Unlicensed money transmitting carries separate US criminal exposure.
cons: This is the provision behind the '1 to 5 times' figure that is often mis-attributed to customers
Severe fines and criminal liability

methods.name: PayPal, Alipay or WeChat Pay outbound personal CNY-to-USD transfer
methods.who: Account holders
methods.how: Use a payment app to send value from a China-linked account to a US account or wallet.
methods.us_tax: Reporting duties attach to the underlying accounts and to any currency gain; they are not avoided by using an app.
cons: No official operator or regulator page confirming an outbound personal CNY-to-USD product, its limits or its fees was verified in this session
Yinfa [2020] No. 330 item 2 supports non-bank payment institutions cooperating with banks for cross-border e-commerce trade flows, which is not the same as a personal capital transfer
Treated as unverified rather than assumed available

methods.name: Reconvert unused RMB back to FX using the original exchange memo
methods.who: A non-domestic individual who previously converted FX into RMB
methods.how: Art. 13(2): unused RMB from an earlier conversion is converted back on presentation of valid ID and the original exchange memo. The memo is valid for reconversion for 24 months from the exchange date. Small same-day amounts up to USD 500 equivalent, and up to USD 1,000 equivalent at pre-departure offsite locations, need ID only.
methods.limit_text: Bounded by the amount originally exchanged; 24-month validity. ID-only tiers: USD 500 per day, or USD 1,000 per day before departure at designated offsite locations.
methods.documents: Valid ID plus the original exchange memo (原兑换水单)
methods.china_cost: Bank FX spread on the reconversion; Bank of China charges no branch exchange fee (S12)
methods.us_tax: Reconversion is a disposition of nonfunctional currency; the IRC 988(e)(2) personal-transaction exclusion applies only where the gain does not exceed USD 200 (S19).
pros: Clean, expressly authorised route for money you originally brought in and converted
Small amounts need ID only
cons: Only works if you kept the original exchange memo
Expires 24 months after the original exchange
Cannot exceed what was originally converted
